e: Yaakov settled
in the land of his father’s residence,
in the land of Canaan.

h: אֵ֣לֶּה תֹּלְד֣וֹת יַעֲקֹ֗ב יוֹסֵ֞ף בֶּן־שְׁבַֽע־עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֨ה רֹעֶ֤ה אֶת־אֶחָיו֙ בַּצֹּ֔אן
וְה֣וּא נַ֗עַר אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י בִלְהָ֛ה וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֖ה נְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֑יו
t: אִלֵּין תּוּלְדַת יַעֲקֹב יוֹסֵף בַּר שְׁבַע עַסְרֵי שְׁנִין (כַּד) הֲוָה רָעֵי עִם אֲחוֹהִי בַּעֲנָא
וְהוּא מְרַבֵּי עִם בְּנֵי בִלְהָה וְעִם בְּנֵי זִלְפָּה נְשֵׁי אֲבוּהִי
וְאַיְתִי יוֹסֵף יָת דִּבְּהוֹן בִּישָׁא לְוַת אֲבוּהוֹן:
e: This is the history of Yaakov; Yoseif at the age of seventeen years, would tend the sheep with his brothers,
and the lad was [he had been raised] with the sons of Bilhah, and the sons of Zilpah, his father’s wives.
Yoseif brought back bad reports about them to their father.

t: וְיִשְׂרָאֵל רְחֵם יָת יוֹסֵף מִכָּל בְּנוֹהִי
e: Yisrael loved Yoseif more than any of his sons,
for he was a [wise] son of his old age to him,
and he made him a long, colorful cloak.

h: וַיִּרְא֣וּ אֶחָ֗יו כִּֽי־אֹת֞וֹ אָהַ֤ב אֲבִיהֶם֙ מִכָּל־אֶחָ֔יו
t: וַחֲזוֹ אֲחוֹהִי אֲרֵי יָתֵיהּ רְחֵם אֲבוּהוֹן מִכָּל אֲחוֹהִי
e: His brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers,
and they hated him.
They could not [were not willing to] speak to him peaceably.
Yoseif had a dream
and he told his brothers,
and they hated him even more.
He said to them,
Listen [now] to this dream that I dreamt.

h: וְ֠הִנֵּה אֲנַ֜חְנוּ מְאַלְּמִ֤ים אֲלֻמִּים֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה
t: וְהָא אֲנַחְנָא מְאַסְּרִין אֱסָרָן בְּגוֹ חַקְלָא
e: Behold, we were binding sheaves in the middle of the field.
Behold my sheaf rose and stood up straight;
and behold your sheaves surrounded it
and prostrated themselves to my sheaf.
His brothers said to him,
Will you then be a king over us? [Do you imagine that you will reign over us?]
Will you indeed rule over us? [Or do you think that you will rule over us?]
They hated him even more
because of his dreams and his words.

h: וְהִנֵּ֧ה הַשֶּׁ֣מֶשׁ וְהַיָּרֵ֗חַ וְאַחַ֤ד עָשָׂר֙ כּֽוֹכָבִ֔ים
t: וְהָא שִׁמְשָׁא וְסִהֲרָא וְחַד עֲשַׂר כּוֹכְבַיָּא
e: He had another dream
and told it to his brothers.
He said, Behold! I dreamed another dream.
The sun, the moon, and eleven stars
were prostrating themselves to me.
He told it to his father and to his brothers.
His father rebuked him,
and said to him,
What is this dream that you dreamed?
Shall I, your mother and your brothers come
and prostrate themselves on the ground to you?
His brothers were jealous of him
but his father kept the matter in mind.
His brothers went off
to pasture their father’s sheep in Shechem.

h: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא אַחֶ֙יךָ֙ רֹעִ֣ים בִּשְׁכֶ֔ם
t: וַאֲמַר יִשְׂרָאֵל לְיוֹסֵף הֲלָא אַחָיךְ רָעָן בִּשְׁכֶם
e: Yisrael said to Yoseif, Aren’t your brothers pasturing [the sheep] in Shechem?
Come, I will send you to them.
He [Yoseif] said to him, Here I am.

h: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ לֶךְ־נָ֨א רְאֵ֜ה אֶת־שְׁל֤וֹם אַחֶ֙יךָ֙ וְאֶת־שְׁל֣וֹם הַצֹּ֔אן
t: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ אִזֵיל כְּעַן חֲזֵי יָת שְׁלָמָא דְאָחוּךְ וְיָת שְׁלָמָא דְעָנָא
e: He [Yisrael] said to him, Go please [now], see after the well-being of your brothers, and the welfare of the sheep,
and bring me a report.
He sent [Yoseif] from the depths [plain] of Chevron,
and he came to Shechem.

t: וּשְׁאָלִנֵּיהּ גַּבְרָא לְמֵימַר מָה אַתְּ בָּעֵי:
e: A man found him
going astray in the field.
The man asked him, What are you seeking?
He said, I am looking for my brothers,
tell me please [now],
where are they pasturing?
The man said, They have traveled on from here,
for I heard them say,
Let us go to Doson.
Yoseif went after his brothers
and found them in Doson.
They saw him from a distance,
and before he approached them
they were plotting against him to kill [thinking about killing] him.
One man said to another,
Here comes the dreamer.

h: וְעַתָּ֣ה לְכ֣וּ וְנַֽהַרְגֵ֗הוּ וְנַשְׁלִכֵ֙הוּ֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד הַבֹּר֔וֹת
t: וּכְעַן אֱתוֹ וְנִקְטְלִנֵּיהּ וְנִרְמִנֵּיהּ בַּחֲדָא מִן גֻּבַּיָּא
e: Now, come let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits;
and we will say that a wild beast devoured him.
Then we will see what will become [be the end] of his dreams.
Reuvein heard
and rescued him from their hands.
He said, Let us not kill him.

h: הַשְׁלִ֣יכוּ אֹת֗וֹ אֶל־הַבּ֤וֹר הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר
t: וַאֲמַר לְהוֹן רְאוּבֵן לָא תוֹשְׁדוּן דְּמָא
רְמוֹ יָתֵיהּ לְגֻבָּא הָדֵין דִּי בְּמַדְבְּרָא
e: Reuvein said to them, Do not commit bloodshed.
Throw him into this pit which is in the wilderness,
and do not lay a hand on him.
His purpose was to rescue him from their hands,
to bring him back to his father.

t: וַהֲוָה כַּד עַל יוֹסֵף לְוַת אֲחוּהִי
e: When Yoseif came to his brothers,
they stripped him of his coat,
the long, colorful coat that he had on.
They took him and threw him into the pit.
The pit was empty;
there was no water in it.
They sat down [reclined] to eat bread.
They raised their eyes and saw —
behold a Yishmaelite [Arabian] caravan
was coming from Gilod.
Their camels were carrying spices, balsam and lotus,
bringing them down to Egypt.

t: מָה מָמוֹן נִתְהֲנֵי לָנָא אֲרֵי נִקְטוֹל יָת אָחוּנָא
e: Yehudah said to his brothers,
What [monetary benefit] will we gain if we kill our brother
and cover up his blood?

t: אֱתוּ וּנְזַבְּנִנֵּיהּ לַעֲרָבָאֵי וִידָנָא לָא תְהֵי בֵיהּ
e: Come let us sell him to the Yishmaelites [Arabs], and let our hands not be upon him;
for he is our brother, our own flesh.
His brothers listened [to him.] [obeyed him].

h: וַיַּֽעַבְרוּ֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים מִדְיָנִ֜ים סֹֽחֲרִ֗ים וַֽיִּמְשְׁכוּ֙ וַיַּֽעֲל֤וּ אֶת־יוֹסֵף֙ מִן־הַבּ֔וֹר
t: וַעֲבָרוּ גַבְרֵי מִדְיָנָאֵי תַּגָּרֵי וּנְגִידוּ וְאַסִּיקוּ יָת יוֹסֵף מִן גֻּבָּא
e: Midianite merchants passed by. They [the brothers] pulled Yoseif up from the pit
and sold Yoseif to the Yishmaelites [Arabs] for twenty pieces of silver.
They brought Yoseif to Egypt.
Reuvein returned to the pit,
but behold, Yoseif was not in the pit.
He [then] tore his clothes [in grief.]
He returned to his brothers and said,
The boy is not there;
and I—where can I go.
They took Yoseif’s coat,
slaughtered a [male] goat,
and dipped the coat in the blood.

t: וְשַׁלָּחוּ יָת כִּתּוּנָא דְפַסֵּי וְאַיְתִיוּ לְוַת אֲבוּהוֹן
אִשְׁתְּמוֹדַע כְּעַן הֲכִתּוּנָא דִבְרָךְ הִיא אִם לָא:
e: They sent the long, colorful coat and brought it to their father,
and said, We found this.
Please [Now] identify it. Is it your son’s coat or not?
He recognized it and said, It is my son’s coat.
An evil beast has devoured him.
Yoseif has been torn to pieces [surely killed].
Yaakov tore his robes,
and placed sackcloth on his loins.
He mourned for his son for many days.

h: וַיָּקֻמוּ֩ כָל־בָּנָ֨יו וְכָל־בְּנֹתָ֜יו לְנַחֲמ֗וֹ וַיְמָאֵן֙ לְהִתְנַחֵ֔ם
t: וְקָמוּ כָל בְּנוֹהִי וְכָל בְּנָתֵיהּ לְנַחֲמוּתֵיהּ וְסָרֵיב לְקַבָּלָא תַנְחוּמִין
וַאֲמַר אֲרֵי אֵחוֹת לְוַת (עַל) בְּרִי כַּד אֲבֵילָא לִשְׁאוֹל
e: All his sons and all his daughters rose to console him, but he refused to be consoled [accept consolation].
He said, I will go down to the grave [while I am still] mourning for my son.
His father wept for him.
The Midianites sold him in Egypt
to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh,
the chief of the slaughterers.

t: וּסְטָא עַד גַּבְרָא עֲדֻלָּמָאָה וּשְׁמֵיהּ חִירָה:
e: And it was at that time,
that Yehudah descended from his brothers.
He turned away [from them], until [he came to] a man, an Adullamite, whose name was Chirah.

h: וַיַּרְא־שָׁ֧ם יְהוּדָ֛ה בַּת־אִ֥ישׁ כְּנַעֲנִ֖י וּשְׁמ֣וֹ שׁ֑וּעַ
t: וַחֲזָא תַמָּן יְהוּדָה בַּת גְּבַר תַּגָּרָא וּשְׁמֵיהּ שׁוּעַ
e: There Yehudah saw the daughter of a Canaanite man [merchant] whose name was Shu’a.
He took her and consummated a marriage with her.
She conceived and gave birth to a son.
He named him Er.
She conceived again and gave birth to a son.
She named him Onan.
She conceived once again and gave birth to a son.
She named him Sheilah.
He [Yehudah] was in Keziv when she gave birth to him.
Yehudah took a wife for Er, his firstborn,
and her name was Tamar.
Er, Yehudah’s firstborn
was wicked in the eyes of [before] Adonoy,
and Adonoy put him to death.

t: עוּל לְוַת אִתַּת אָחוּךְ וְיַבֵּם יָתַהּ
e: Yehudah said to Onan,
Consummate marriage with your brother’s wife, and fulfill the yibum rite with her,
and establish seed for your brother.

h: וְהָיָ֞ה אִם־בָּ֨א אֶל־אֵ֤שֶׁת אָחִיו֙ וְשִׁחֵ֣ת אַ֔רְצָה
t: וַהֲוָה כַּד עֲלִיל לְוַת אִתַּת אֲחוּהִי וּמְחַבֵּל אָרְחֵיהּ עַל אַרְעָא
e: Onan knew
that the descendants would not be his [called by his name].
Whenever he cohabited with his brother’s wife, he let it go to waste [destroyed his way] on the ground,
in order not to give [establish] progeny to his brother.
What he did was evil in the eyes of [before] Adonoy,
and He also put him to death.

h: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָה֩ לְתָמָ֨ר כַּלָּת֜וֹ שְׁבִ֧י אַלְמָנָ֣ה בֵית־אָבִ֗יךְ עַד־יִגְדַּל֙ שֵׁלָ֣ה בְנִ֔י
t: וַאֲמַר יְהוּדָה לְתָמָר כַּלְּתֵיהּ תִּיבִי אַרְמְלָא בֵית אָבִיךְ עַד דִּרְבָא שֵׁלָה בְרִי
e: Yehudah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law, Live as a widow in your father’s house until my son Sheilah is of age.
He said,
Lest he also die like his brothers.
Tamar went
and lived in her father’s house.

h: וַיִּנָּ֣חֶם יְהוּדָ֗ה וַיַּ֜עַל עַל־גֹּֽזֲזֵ֤י צֹאנוֹ֙ ה֗וּא וְחִירָ֛ה רֵעֵ֥הוּ הָעֲדֻלָּמִ֖י תִּמְנָֽתָה׃
t: וְאִתְנַחֵם יְהוּדָה וּסְלִיק עַל גּוֹזְזֵי עָנֵיהּ הוּא וְחִירָה רַחֲמֵיהּ עֲדֻלָּמָאָה לְתִמְנָת:
e: Many days passed,
and Shu’a’s daughter, the wife of Yehudah died.
Yehudah sought consolation, and went up to his sheep-shearers—he and his friend, Chirah the Adullamite—to Timnah.

h: הִנֵּ֥ה חָמִ֛יךְ עֹלֶ֥ה תִמְנָ֖תָה לָגֹ֥ז צֹאנֽוֹ׃
t: הָא חֲמוּיִךְ סָלֵק לְתִמְנָת לְמֵיגַז עָנֵיהּ:
e: Tamar was told,
Behold your father-in-law has come to Timnah, to shear his sheep.

h: וַתָּסַר֩ בִּגְדֵ֨י אַלְמְנוּתָ֜הּ מֵֽעָלֶ֗יהָ וַתְּכַ֤ס בַּצָּעִיף֙ וַתִּתְעַלָּ֔ף
t: וְאַעְדִּיאַת לְבוּשֵׁי אַרְמְלוּתַהּ מִנַּהּ וְאִתְכַּסִּיאַת בְּעֵיפָא וְאִתַּקָּנַת
e: She took off her widow’s garb, covered herself with a veil, and disguised [adorned] herself.
She sat at the crossroads
which is on the road to Timnah,
for she saw that Sheilah had come of age
and she had not been given to him for a wife.
Yehudah saw her
and thought she was a harlot [like one who goes outside],
because she had covered her face.

h: וַיֵּ֨ט אֵלֶ֜יהָ אֶל־הַדֶּ֗רֶךְ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽבָה־נָּא֙ אָב֣וֹא אֵלַ֔יִךְ
t: וּסְטָא לְוָתַהּ לְאָרְחָא וַאֲמַר הָבִי כְעַן אֵיעוֹל לְוָתִיךְ
e: He turned aside to her on the road, and said, Please [Now], let me be with you,
for he did not know
that she was his daughter-in-law.
She said, What will you give me
for the privilege of being with me?

t: וַאֲמַר אֲנָא אֲשַׁלַּח גַּדְיָא בַר עִזֵּי מִן עָנָא
וַאֲמֶרֶת אִם תִּתֵּן מַשְׁכּוֹנָא עַד דְּתִשְׁלָח:
e: He said, I will send you a kid from the flock.
She said, [Only] if you give me some security until you send it.

t: וַאֲמַר מָה מַשְׁכּוֹנָא דִּי אֶתֵּן לָךְ
וִיהַב לַהּ וְעַל לְוָתַהּ וְעַדִּיאַת לֵיהּ:
e: He said, What security shall I give you?
She said, Your signet ring, your wrap,
and your staff that is in your hand.
He gave them to her and was with her, and she became pregnant by him.
She got up and went away.
She took off her veil,
and put on her widow’s garb.

h: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יְהוּדָ֜ה אֶת־גְּדִ֣י הָֽעִזִּ֗ים בְּיַד֙ רֵעֵ֣הוּ הָֽעֲדֻלָּמִ֔י
t: וְשַׁדַּר יְהוּדָה יָת גַּדְיָא בַר עִזֵּי בִּידָא רַחֲמֵיהּ עֲדֻלָּמָאָה
e: Yehudah sent the goat-kid with his friend the Adullamite,
to retrieve the security from the woman,
but he could not find her.

t: אָן מְקַדִּשְׁתָּא הִיא בְעַיְנִין עַל אָרְחָא
e: He asked the men of her place,
Where is the harlot that was at the junction, on the road?
They said, There was [is] no harlot here.
He returned to Yehudah
and said, I did not find her,
and the men of her place also said
that there was [is] no harlot there [here].
Yehudah said, Let her take it,
lest we are humiliated [become a laughingstock].
Behold I sent her this kid,
and you could not find her.

h: וַיְהִ֣י כְּמִשְׁלֹ֣שׁ חֳדָשִׁ֗ים וַיֻּגַּ֨ד לִֽיהוּדָ֤ה לֵֽאמֹר֙ זָֽנְתָה֙ תָּמָ֣ר כַּלָּתֶ֔ךָ
t: וַהֲוָה כִּתְלָתוּת יַרְחַיָּא וְאִתְחַוָּא לִיהוּדָה לְמֵימַר זַנִּיאַת תָּמָר כַּלְּתָךְ
e: About three months later, Yehudah was told, Tamar, your daughter-in-law, has been promiscuous,
moreover, her promiscuity has resulted in pregnancy.
Yehudah said,
Take her out and let her be burned.

h: הִ֣וא מוּצֵ֗את וְהִ֨יא שָׁלְחָ֤ה אֶל־חָמִ֙יהָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
t: הִיא מִתַּפְּקָא וְהִיא שְׁלָחַת לַחֲמוּהָא לְמֵימַר
e: She was being taken out, and she sent [word] to her father-in-law saying,
By the man to whom these belong
[from him] am I pregnant.
She said,
Please [Now] recognize to whom this signet, wrap and staff belong.

t: אֲרֵי עַל כֵּן לָא יְהָבִתַּהּ לְשֵׁלָה בְרִי
e: Yehudah recognized them and said, She is righteous, [it is] from me [that she conceived],
inasmuch that I did not give her to my son Sheilah.
He was not intimate with her any more.
When the time came for her to give birth,
there were twins in her womb.

h: וַתִּקַּ֣ח הַמְיַלֶּ֗דֶת וַתִּקְשֹׁ֨ר עַל־יָד֤וֹ שָׁנִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
t: וּנְסִיבַת חַיְתָא וּקְטָרַת עַל יְדֵיהּ זְהוֹרִיתָא לְמֵימַר
e: As she was giving birth, one of them put out his hand.
The midwife took it and tied a scarlet thread on his hand, saying,
This one emerged first.

h: וַיְהִ֣י כְּמֵשִׁ֣יב יָד֗וֹ וְהִנֵּה֙ יָצָ֣א אָחִ֔יו
t: וַהֲוָה כַּד אֲתֵיב יְדֵיהּ וְהָא נְפַק אֲחוּהִי
e: When he put back his hand, behold his brother emerged,
and she said, With what [great] strength you have pushed yourself.
He named him Peretz.
Then his brother emerged —
the one upon whose hand was the scarlet thread.
He named him Zorach.

h: וַיִּקְנֵ֡הוּ פּוֹטִיפַר֩ סְרִ֨יס פַּרְעֹ֜ה שַׂ֤ר הַטַּבָּחִים֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י
t: וּזְבָנֵיהּ פּוֹטִיפַר רַבָּא דְפַרְעֹה רַב קָטוֹלַיָּא גְּבַר מִצְרָאָה
e: Yoseif was brought down to Egypt.
He was purchased by Potiphar — an officer of Pharaoh, the chief of the slaughterers, an Egyptian —
from the Yishmaelites [Arabs]
who had brought him down there.
[The Word of] Adonoy was with Yoseif[’s support],
and he was successful.
He was [a servant] in the house of his master, the Egyptian.
His master saw
that [the Word of] Adonoy was with him [supported him],
and that whatever he did,
Adonoy made it succeed through his hand.

h: וַיִּמְצָ֨א יוֹסֵ֥ף חֵ֛ן בְּעֵינָ֖יו וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹת֑וֹ
t: וְאַשְׁכַּח יוֹסֵף רַחֲמִין בְּעֵינוֹהִי וְשַׁמֵּשׁ יָתֵיהּ
וְכָל דִּי אִית לֵיהּ מְסַר בִּידֵיהּ:
e: Yoseif found favor in his eyes, and he served him personally.
He appointed him supervisor over his household,
and all that he possessed he placed in his hand.

h: וַיְהִ֡י מֵאָז֩ הִפְקִ֨יד אֹת֜וֹ בְּבֵית֗וֹ וְעַל֙ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ל֔וֹ
וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית הַמִּצְרִ֖י בִּגְלַ֣ל יוֹסֵ֑ף
t: וַהֲוָה מֵעִדַּן דְּמַנֵּי יָתֵיהּ בְּבֵיתֵיהּ וְעַל כָּל דִּי אִית לֵיהּ
וּבָרִיךְ יְיָ יָת בֵּית מִצְרָאָה בְּדִיל יוֹסֵף
וַהֲוָה בִּרְכְּתָא דַיְיָ בְּכָל דִּי אִית לֵיהּ
e: From the time he appointed him supervisor over his household and over all that he possessed,
Adonoy blessed the house of the Egyptian for Yoseif’s sake.
The blessing of Adonoy was in all that he possessed, in the house
and in the field.

t: וּשְׁבַק כָּל דִּי לֵיהּ בִּידָא דְיוֹסֵף
וַהֲוָה יוֹסֵף שַׁפִּיר בְּרֵיוָא וְיָאֵי בְחֶזְוָא:
e: He left everything he possessed in the hand of Yoseif.
He did not concern himself with anything about him,
except for the bread he ate.
Yoseif was well-built and good looking.

t: וּזְקָפַת אִתַּת רִבּוֹנֵיהּ יָת עֵינָהָא לְיוֹסֵף
e: After these events,
his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Yoseif,
and she said, Be with me.

t: וְכָל דִּי אִית לֵיהּ מְסַר בִּידִי:
e: He refused
and said to his master’s wife,
Behold, my master
knows nothing about what I am doing in the house,
and all that he possess, he has placed in my hands.
No one in this house is greater than me.
He has not withheld anything from me
other than you, for you are his wife.
How can I do such a great evil,
and sin against [before] God.

h: וְלֹא־שָׁמַ֥ע אֵלֶ֛יהָ לִשְׁכַּ֥ב אֶצְלָ֖הּ לִהְי֥וֹת עִמָּֽהּ׃
t: וַהֲוָה כַּד מַלֵּילַת עִם יוֹסֵף יוֹם יוֹם
וְלָא קַבִּיל מִנַּהּ לְמִשְׁכַּב לְוָתַהּ לְמֶהֱוֵי עִמַּהּ:
e: Even though she spoke to Yoseif every day,
he would not listen to [obey] her, to lie next to her, [nor] to be with her.

h: וְאֵ֨ין אִ֜ישׁ מֵאַנְשֵׁ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת שָׁ֖ם בַּבָּֽיִת׃
t: וְלֵית אֱנַשׁ מֵאֲנָשֵׁי בֵיתָא תַּמָּן בְּבֵיתָא:
e: It was on such a day,
that he came to the house to do his work [examine the recordings of his accounts].
No man of the household was there in the house.
She grabbed him by his garment, saying, Be with me.
He left his garment in her hand,
and fled, and he went outside [to the marketplace].
It was when she saw
that he left his garment in her hand
and had fled outside [to the marketplace],

h: וַתִּקְרָ֞א לְאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵיתָ֗הּ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
רְא֗וּ הֵ֥בִיא לָ֛נוּ אִ֥ישׁ עִבְרִ֖י לְצַ֣חֶק בָּ֑נוּ
t: וּקְרַת לַאֲנָשֵׁי בֵיתַהּ וַאֲמֶרֶת לְהוֹן לְמֵימַר
חֲזוֹ אַיְתִי לָנָא גַּבְרָא עִבְרָאָה לְחַיָּכָא בָנָא
e: that she called to the men of the household and said to them,
See, he brought us a Hebrew man to mock us.
He came to be with me,
and I called out in a loud voice.
When he heard
that I raised my voice and cried out,
he left his garment with me,
and fled and went outside [to the marketplace].
She laid his garment near her
until his master came home.

h: בָּֽא־אֵלַ֞י הָעֶ֧בֶד הָֽעִבְרִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־הֵבֵ֥אתָ לָּ֖נוּ לְצַ֥חֶק בִּֽי׃
t: עַל לְוָתִי עַבְדָא עִבְרָאָה דִּי אַיְתֵיתָא לָנָא לְחַיָּכָא בִי:
e: She spoke to him
[her husband] according to these words,
saying, The Hebrew slave came to me — the same one you brought into us — [he came to] mock me.
When I raised my voice and cried out,
he left his garment with me and fled outside [to the marketplace].

h: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲדֹנָ֜יו אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֣י אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבְּרָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
t: וַהֲוָה כַד שְׁמַע רִבּוֹנֵיהּ יָת פִּתְגָּמֵי אִתְּתֵיהּ דִּי מַלֵּילַת עִמֵּיהּ לְמֵימַר
e: When his master heard the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying,
Your slave did such things to me,
he became furious.

h: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֲדֹנֵ֨י יוֹסֵ֜ף אֹת֗וֹ וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֔הַר
t: וּנְסִיב רִבּוֹנֵיהּ דְּיוֹסֵף יָתֵיהּ וּמַנְּיֵהּ לְבֵית אֲסִירֵי
e: Yoseif’s master took him and placed him in [appointed him over] the prison,
the place where the king’s prisoners were jailed.
He remained there in the prison.
[The Word of] Adonoy was with Yoseif[’s support],
and extended kindness to him,
granting him favor
in the eyes of the prison chief.
The prison chief gave [appointed] Yoseif [to be in] control over
all the prisoners
in the prison,
and everything that had to be done there,
he was the one who did it [it was done by his word].

h: אֵ֣ין שַׂ֣ר בֵּית־הַסֹּ֗הַר רֹאֶ֤ה אֶֽת־כָּל־מְא֙וּמָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ
t: לֵית רַב בֵּית אֲסִירֵי חָזֵי יָת כָּל סָרְחָן בִּידֵיהּ
e: The prison chief did not have to look after anything that was under [see any offense committed by] his hand,
because [the Word of] Adonoy was with him [his support]
and whatever he did, Adonoy made him succeed.
After these events,
an offense was committed by the Egyptian king’s butler and baker
against their master, the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh was enraged
at his two officials,
the chief butler
and the chief baker.

h: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתָ֜ם בְּמִשְׁמַ֗ר בֵּ֛ית שַׂ֥ר הַטַבָּחִ֖ים אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר
t: וִיהַב יָתְהוֹן בְּמַטְּרָא בֵּית רַב קָטוֹלַיָּא לְבֵית אֲסִירֵי
e: He placed them under guard in the house of the chief executioner, in the prison,
where Yoseif was imprisoned.

h: וַ֠יִּפְקֹד שַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֧ים אֶת־יוֹסֵ֛ף אִתָּ֖ם וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹתָ֑ם
t: וּמַנִּי רַב קָטוֹלַיָּא יָת יוֹסֵף עִמְּהוֹן וְשַׁמֵּשׁ יָתְהוֹן
e: The chief of the slaughterers appointed Yoseif to be with them and he served them.
They were under guard for a period of time.

h: וַיַּֽחַלְמוּ֩ חֲל֨וֹם שְׁנֵיהֶ֜ם אִ֤ישׁ חֲלֹמוֹ֙ בְּלַ֣יְלָה אֶחָ֔ד
t: וַחֲלָמוּ חֶלְמָא תַּרְוֵיהוֹן גְּבַר חֶלְמֵיהּ בְּלֵילְיָא חַד
e: The two of them had a dream. Each of them had his dream on the same night,
each man according to the interpretation of his dream,
the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt,
who were imprisoned in the prison.
Yoseif came to them in the morning,
and he saw them,
and behold they were troubled.

h: וַיִּשְׁאַ֞ל אֶת־סְרִיסֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אִתּ֧וֹ בְמִשְׁמַ֛ר בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר
t: וּשְׁאֵל יָת רַבְרְבֵי פַרְעֹה דִּי עִמֵּיהּ בְּמַטְּרָא בֵּית רִבּוֹנֵיהּ לְמֵימָר
מָא דֵין אַפֵּיכוֹן בִּישִׁין יוֹמָא דֵין:
e: He asked Pharaoh’s officials, who were with him, under guard in his master’s house, saying,
Why do you look so bad today?

h: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא לֵֽאלֹהִים֙ פִּתְרֹנִ֔ים
t: וַאֲמַר לְהוֹן יוֹסֵף הֲלָא מִן קֳדָם יְיָ פּוּשְׁרַן חֶלְמַיָּא
e: They said to him,
We had a dream,
and there is no interpreter of it.
Yoseif said to them, Do not [Are] interpretations [of dreams] belong to [not from] God.
Tell them to me, please [now].

t: וְאִשְׁתָּעִי רַב שָׁקֵי יָת חֶלְמֵיהּ לְיוֹסֵף
e: The butler told his dream to Yoseif.
He said to him,
In my dream, behold a grape vine was before me.
On the vine there were three branches,
as [when] if budding, [it brought out blossoms and] its [the] blossoms blooming,
and its clusters ripening into grapes.

h: וָאֶקַּ֣ח אֶת־הָֽעֲנָבִ֗ים וָֽאֶשְׂחַ֤ט אֹתָם֙ אֶל־כּ֣וֹס פַּרְעֹ֔ה
t: וּנְסֵיבִת יָת עִנְּבַיָּא וְעַצָּרִית יָתְהוֹן לְכַסָּא דְפַרְעֹה
וִיהָבִית יָת כַּסָּא עַל יְדָא דְפַרְעֹה:
e: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand.
I took the grapes and squeezed them into Pharaoh’s cup.
I then placed the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.
Yoseif said to him,
This is its interpretation:
The three branches
are three days.

h: בְּע֣וֹד שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֤א פַרְעֹה֙ אֶת־רֹאשֶׁ֔ךָ
e: In another [At the end of] three days, Pharaoh will lift [take] your head,
and restore you to your position.
You will place Pharaoh’s cup in his hand,
as was your previous practice
when you were his butler.

h: כִּ֧י אִם־זְכַרְתַּ֣נִי אִתְּךָ֗ כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ
t: אֶלָּהֵן תִּדְכְּרִנַּנִי עִמָּךְ כַּד יֵיטַב לָךְ
e: But remember me when things go well with you.
Please [Now] deal kindly with me [with goodness],
and mention me to [before] Pharaoh,
and take me out of this house [prison].
I was kidnaped
from the land of the Hebrews,
and here I have also done nothing
that they should have put me in this dungeon [prison].

t: וַחֲזָא רַב נַחְתּוֹמֵי אֲרֵי יָאוּת פָּשַׁר
וְהָא תְּלָתָא סַלִּין דְּחִירוּ עַל רֵישִׁי:
e: The chief baker saw that he interpreted well.
He said to Yoseif,
I, too, dreamed.
Behold there were three fancy baskets on my head.

h: וְהָע֗וֹף אֹכֵ֥ל אֹתָ֛ם מִן־הַסַּ֖ל מֵעַ֥ל רֹאשִֽׁי׃
t: וְעוֹפָא אָכֵל יָתְהוֹן מִן סַלָּא מֵעִלָּוֵי רֵישִׁי:
e: In the top basket
there were various kinds of food for Pharaoh, consisting of baked goods,
and the bird was eating them from the basket that was on my head.
Yoseif replied and said,
This is its interpretation:
The three baskets
represent three days.

h: בְּע֣וֹד שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֨א פַרְעֹ֤ה אֶת־רֹֽאשְׁךָ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ
t: בְּסוֹף תְּלָתָא יוֹמִין יַעְדִּי פַרְעֹה יָת רֵישָׁךְ מִנָּךְ
e: In another [At the end of] three days, Pharaoh will lift [remove] your head from off you.
He will hang you on a tree,
and the bird will eat your flesh from off you.

h: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י י֚וֹם הֻלֶּ֣דֶת אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֔ה
וַיִּשָּׂ֞א אֶת־רֹ֣אשׁ שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֗ים וְאֶת־רֹ֛אשׁ שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ עֲבָדָֽיו׃
t: וַהֲוָה בְּיוֹמָא תְלִיתָאָה יוֹמָא בֵּית וַלְדָא דְפַרְעֹה
וְאִדְכַּר יָת רֵישׁ רַב שָׁקֵי וְיָת רֵישׁ רַב נַחְתּוֹמֵי בְּגוֹ עַבְדּוֹהִי:
e: It was on the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday,
that he [Pharaoh] made a feast for all his servants.
He lifted [remembered] the head of the chief butler, and the head of the chief baker among his servants.

t: וַאֲתֵיב יָת רַב שָׁקֵי עַל שַׁקְיוּתֵיהּ
וִיהַב יָת כַּסָּא עַל יְדָא דְפַרְעֹה:
e: He restored the chief butler to his position,
and he presented the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.
The chief baker, he hung,
just as Yoseif had interpreted to them.

t: וְלָא דְכִיר רַב שָׁקֵי יָת יוֹסֵף וְאַנְשְׁיֵהּ:
e: [However] the chief butler did not remember Yoseif, but forgot him.
